reviewer: Specialist: life_safety, accessibility, acoustics_av (other disciplines not scored)
weighted_score_note: Weighted over the three assigned disciplines only (15/10/10, normalised to 35). Not comparable to a full nine-discipline score. Iter-01 (B01) was 4.29.
iter01_blocker_status: RESOLVED geometrically. I verified this in the manifest. ARC-WALL-BOH-CORRIDOR has openings at x 19.6-23.2 and 65.9-69.5 (z 0-2.4). Each opening leads into an exit passage that is 3.6 m wide between its walls (ARC-WALL-BOH-EXIT-W1/W2 at x 19.45-19.6 / 23.2-23.35 and E1/E2, y 55.3-60.85), and each passage ends at a final exit in the north wall: DR-EXT-BOH-W (21.4, 61.0) and DR-EXT-BOH-E (67.7, 61.0), each 3.36 m effective. These line up with DR-STAGE-W/E at y 52.0. The route passes through no room doors. EGR-09 confirms it (via [], doors_fire_exit true) and EGR-08 confirms the loads (BOH-W 617, BOH-E 390). The remaining weakness is that the passages and the corridor crossing have no fire separation (B02-LS-03).

findings.finding: This is still the main egress weakness and it has not improved: about two thirds of hall occupants leave from the rear passage, which is now higher at +3.325 m (was +2.98), and must go down stairs. 2,326 of 3,497 hall occupants (66.5 %) use the six L02 exits. The two side-foyer exits are loaded exactly to their stair capacity (400 occupants each on 3.0 m), so there is no margin.
findings.evidence: exit_schedule.csv: W-REAR 157, E-REAR 181, S1 588, S2 600, ARC-W 400 (capacity 3.0 = required 3.0), ARC-E 400 (3.0 / 3.0); metrics top_level 3.325; L00 exits carry 121 + 73 + 602 + 375.
findings.fix: Add grade exits through the side walls at the ends of the cross-aisle passage. The new cross-end ramps already bring people down to grade at about y 43-49, so these exits would take load off the L02 stairs. Aim for no more than about half of the occupants on stairs, with at least 10 % spare capacity on every stair.

findings.finding: Travel distances are worse than in B01. 486 occupants are beyond the 30 m in-hall flag (was 406) and the maximum is 43.73 m (was 41.6 m). The direct seat-to-exit maximum is 31.53 m, against 26.1 m for Option A. The engine still measures the final legs as straight lines and adds a fixed allowance for stairs.
findings.evidence: geometry_checks EGR-03 {max 43.73, over_flag 486}, EGR-03N {43.73, 410}; comparison.md direct seat-to-exit max 31.53 (A 26.1).
findings.fix: Use the same extra grade exits at the ends of the cross aisle to shorten travel for the side blocks, and measure the final legs on a route graph.

findings.finding: The stage-side escape route still crosses the open 3 m BOH corridor. The corridor-wall openings at the exit passages have no doors, and the corridor has room doors opening onto it, including the plant room (DR-BOH-08) and the stores. About 1,000 people, plus all 60 wheelchair users and companions (ACC-08 assigns them only to DR-STAGE-W/E), depend on a route whose separation is 'TBC'. The hall-door Role text still calls it a 'protected route'.
findings.evidence: manifest ARC-WALL-BOH-EXIT-* 'fire separation TBC'; corridor-wall openings 19.6-23.2 / 65.9-69.5 with no IfcDoor; DR-BOH-08 at (74.68, 55.22); DR-STAGE-W/E props Role '...protected route to BOH exits'; egress_travel.csv: wheelchair and companion exits 36 to DR-STAGE-W and 24 to DR-STAGE-E; ACC-08 value [DR-STAGE-E, DR-STAGE-W].
findings.fix: Put fire doors (or a lobby) at the corridor openings so that each exit passage is a separated route from the hall door to outside. Alternatively, cross the corridor in a short protected lobby. Remove 'protected' from the Role text until the separation is designed. Let wheelchair users also use the grade front-corner exits (DR-HALL-W/E-FRONT, which carry only 121 and 73 people) so their evacuation does not depend on the BOH route alone.

findings.finding: Adding the ramps narrowed the cross-aisle end steps to 0.73 m (4 risers of 0.131 m). These steps are part of the descent for ambulant people from the cross aisle to the stage and front exits, which carry about 92 rear-section occupants plus the wheelchair users and companions. Each end has 2.33 m in total (0.73 m stair + 1.6 m ramp), but a 0.73 m stair is below the usual minimum for an egress stair, and steps and ramp side by side invite trips.
findings.evidence: manifest ARC-STAIR-CROSS-W/E Width 0.73, Risers 4, Riser 0.131; ARC-RAMP-CROSS-W/E width 1.6, run 6.3, rise 0.525; egress_travel.csv rear-row seats to DR-STAGE/FRONT: 92.
findings.fix: Drop the steps and widen each ramp to about 2.4 m (it is 1:12, so ambulant people can use it too), or widen the stair to at least 1.2 m with handrails on both sides and a contrasting edge.

findings.finding: The other stair fixes are confirmed. All L02 stairs are now 2 flights (at most 10 risers per flight, CIR-06), the 6 m foyer stairs have centre handrails, and the ambulatory is 5.0 m wide with a 2.0 m stair, leaving about 2.9 m clear beside it. The riser is now 0.175 m, which is exactly the placeholder maximum.
findings.evidence: geometry_checks CIR-06 {max_risers_per_flight 10, max_flights 2}; stairs ARC-STAIR-AMB-W bbox x -5.5 to -3.5 against the hall wall at -0.45; CIR-05 risers 0.175.
findings.fix: None required at concept stage. Keep the riser below the local limit once the code is known.

findings.finding: The front wheelchair places are fixed: they are now in rows 1-2 of the centre blocks, about 7 m from the pulpit and close to its axis. The outermost band groups, however, are still about 81-83 deg off the pulpit axis, which is beyond the 80 deg bearing now used to trim congregation seats. Wheelchair positions are still not included in the bearing check.
findings.fix: Move the M01 and M12 places one or two groups towards the centre, and run the bearing and SGT-H1 checks over wheelchair positions as well.

findings.finding: There is now a genuinely step-free route: front-corner door at grade, then the cross-end ramp (1:12, 0.525 m rise, 6.3 m single run, 1.6 m wide), the cross-aisle passage, the band ramp (0.10 m), and the band itself. ACC-08 keeps wheelchair users on exits at grade. But the 1.6 m ramp is shared with ambulant people coming down beside the 0.73 m steps, and its edge protection and handrails are not modelled.
findings.fix: Widen the ramp (see B02-LS-04) and model handrails and kerbs.

findings.finding: This is unchanged from B01: the lift serves L02, but there are no refuge spaces at the six L02 stair heads, and no wheelchair places on L02.
findings.evidence: manifest contains no REFUGE elements; accessible_positions.csv has 30 places, none on L02.
findings.fix: Add refuge spaces with two-way communication at the foyer stair heads, or state that L02 is a staff/booth-only level for wheelchair users.

findings.finding: The choir is now on 0.2 m tiers up to +0.80 m. The wheelchair choir place stays at grade, so the tiers need guarding and an accessible route only for that one row. Choir occupants (377) route to the front-corner and stage doors across the tiers, and stepped tiers in a side zone add some evacuation risk.
findings.evidence: params stage.choir._iteration2; egress_travel.csv choir exits W-FRONT 121, STAGE-E 117, E-FRONT 73, STAGE-W 66.
findings.fix: Model the tier edges, guards and step nosings, and keep a level 1.2 m route along the grade row to both choir exits.

findings.finding: Changing the rear wall to 5 deg facets (each about 3.97 m long) makes the wall a closer approximation to a true concave arc centred on the platform focus. That makes focusing slightly worse, not better. The absorptive finish is an allowance in params only; it is not a modelled element or a stated performance requirement, and the infill above the wall is still missing.
findings.evidence: manifest ARC-WALL-ARC-W-01..08 Length 3.97, Description 'Faceted hall wall...'; params rear_corners.arc_wall_facet_deg 5.0 and _acoustics allowance; open_issues.md 'focused-echo risk to be checked by an acoustician'.
findings.fix: Set a performance requirement, for example a broadband-absorptive or 1-2 m scale diffusing finish over the full height, including the infill up to the roof. Alternatively, tilt the facets so that each reflects down into the rear rows. Record the allowance as a modelled covering element (IfcCovering) with that requirement.

findings.finding: The volume is 10.05 m3 per seat (30,149 m3), which still suits amplified worship. Narrowing the fan reduces side-on seats from 320 to 228 (more than 75 deg) and the maximum bearing to 80 deg. However, 1,572 seats now rely on screens (was 1,398), and screen viewing is still checked only for horizontal angle and distance. There is no loudspeaker coverage check and no RT estimate.
findings.evidence: comparison.md volume 30,149 m3 / 10.05 per seat, seats > 75 deg 228, max bearing 80.0; SGT-H1 relying_on_screens 1572.
findings.fix: Add a check of vertical viewing angle and of obstructions (trusses, choir tiers) to SGT-H1. Run a simple direct-sound coverage map and an early RT estimate.

strengths: The iter-01 critical blocker is resolved. The stage-side exits now discharge straight through dedicated 3.6 m passages to external doors aligned with them, and the new explicit discharge-route check EGR-09 would catch any route that passes through a room.
Every egress stair now has a landing (flights of at most 10 risers), the wide stairs have centre handrails, and the ambulatory stair no longer squeezes the step-free route.
There is a real step-free route to and from the wheelchair band, and wheelchair users are restricted to exits at grade (ACC-08).
The front wheelchair places now have central, close views of the pulpit.
The hall has 10 exits with 34.8 m of capacity width against a 23.3 m placeholder demand, and no occupant exceeds the 60 m total travel flag.
limitations: Corridor openings, passage walls and door positions were verified from the manifest matrices and mesh vertices. The 'about 1,000 people' in B02-LS-03 is the sum of the two stage-door loads (602 + 375); I did not separately check the corridor's capacity for that flow. I did not rebuild the egress on a route graph, did no acoustic modelling, and did not review the B02 renders in detail. All criteria are placeholders because no local code values are available. Option A was not re-reviewed (unchanged).
certification_disclaimer: This is a concept-stage QA review score. It is not professional certification, fire/egress approval, accessibility audit, acoustic design or code-compliance confirmation; a qualified fire engineer, access consultant and acoustician must review the design under applicable Zimbabwean requirements.
